brief: The note frames global bond stress as Hemingway's 'gradually, then suddenly': a weak 5-year auction (5.0% yield) and 7-year (5.1%), with indirect bidders down to 54% of the 5-year from 61.5%, alongside UK gilts at 5.3% and French OATs spreading over 100bps versus Bunds. It argues the yield rise is less about oil than growth and competition for capital, because hyperscaler AI financing needs ($1.7-2.1T of credit-market supply, pushing 2026-27 IG issuance toward $3.9-4.0T) are landing in the same market as Treasury supply. Credit shows hidden stress: HY breadth is deteriorating despite a still-tight OAS, and private-credit funds (Morgan Stanley, Blackstone, Cliffwater) are gating redemptions though the underlying loans have not defaulted. Equities report weak internals (under 50% of S&P above the 200-day average) despite index highs. Meta's Muse launch drove a stock pop but the note expects rivals to ship copies within six months, turning it into a subsidized margin war; Meta is expected to follow Alphabet's capital raise with its own before Anthropic's listing. Separately, Hormuz oil flows have recovered but refined-product (diesel) capacity remains constrained, with a US export ban risking a further price spike abroad.
